The base template: menus, death and fallbacks

New games are seeded with editable boilerplate before the first room. Use it as a recommended starting point when it fits, or extend or replace any part to serve the brief. These are ordinary game resources, with no protected ownership or reserved template ranges.

- Logic 0 builds the menu bar once on boot (File: Save, Restore, Restart, Quit; Speed; Sound; Help), binds the classic keys (ESC opens the menu, F5/F7/F9 save, restore and restart, F1 shows help, TAB lists the inventory), turns the status line on, then runs call.v(v0) so your room logic runs first every cycle. After the room returns, logic 0 answers the menu controllers and, once per submitted line, prints the parser fallback: "I don't know the word" when the line carried an unknown word, "I don't understand that" when no said() matched. A room that answers a line without a said() match should set(f4) after its own reply so the template does not add the generic one.
- Death is a shared handler: print your death line, then call(255). It stops input and movement, plays the death sound and offers the Restore, Restart or Quit box — SPACE steps the choice, ENTER confirms, 1-3 choose directly, F7/F9/Alt-Z answer directly. A cancelled or failed restore returns to the box; the player stays dead rather than walking in a broken control mode. If you replace this handler, design and playtest the recovery or continuation behavior your game needs.
- Read logic 0 and logic 255 for their current state, controller and string usage before editing; their sources are available through read_logic. Update affected references together when reusing IDs or changing conventions. Automatic allocation avoids IDs used by the current code; explicit bindings and edits can coordinate a rewrite. Playtest boot, input and any menu/death behavior affected by your changes. A fair death still needs a fair cause: the hazard belongs in your room's picture and priority plane.

rooms.title: Castle Gate
rooms.description: Opening room. Thornwall's gray gatehouse across a drawbridge over the moat. Wenna takes the king's notice from the board (accepts the errand, +10) and finds a bent brass hook behind it; bread and a lit brass lantern wait on a supply crate. An alligator watches from the moat: swimming warns once, then kills. Smoke rises from a crooked chimney in the eastern hills.

rooms.title: Great Hall
rooms.description: King Brannoc waits beside the last candle of Thornwall. He explains the Three Bright Things and hints where each lies. Bringing the Bell, Ember and Map together restores the kingdom (+60) and ends the story.

rooms.title: Meadow and Old Oak
rooms.description: A crossroads meadow. An old woman knits map-thread under an old oak beside a talking well. Talking kindly earns a ball of yarn; answering her riddle (answer: candle) earns the Map (+40). The well gives hints. Roadside candle #1 can be lit with the lantern.

rooms.name: unused
rooms.title: Riverbank
rooms.description: A heron stands in the shallows and would like to discuss the bread first. Giving it the bread earns passage along the river (+20): it shows Wenna the stepping stones upriver to the gorge. Roadside candle #2 stands here.

rooms.title: River Gorge
rooms.description: A deep pool under a waterfall. The Bell lies tangled at the bottom and rings faintly under water. Diving fails; Wenna ties the brass hook to the yarn and fishes the Bell up (+40).

rooms.title: Stove Hut
rooms.description: A hill hut with a crooked smoking chimney. A vain salamander lives in the stove and keeps the undying Ember. It is impressed by polished brass: show it the lantern after polishing it (polish lantern) and it trades the Ember (+40). Roadside candle #3 stands by the door.

messages: The last candle in Thornwall burns in the great hall, and when it goes out, so does the kingdom. You are Wenna, third squire to King Brannoc. This morning the king posted a notice at the gate.

The gate of Thornwall Castle. A drawbridge crosses the moat to the great hall. The king's notice hangs on a board by the moat, and someone has left supplies on a crate. The path runs east into the meadow. Something in the moat is watching you.
You unpin the notice and tuck it into your tunic. The errand is yours now. Behind where it hung, a bent brass hook sticks out of the board.
You work the brass hook loose. It is bent into a neat curl, like the end of a fishing line.
You take the loaf of bread. It smells good enough to be a problem.
You take the lantern. Its flame does not even flicker.
You rub the lantern with your oversized sleeve until the soot comes off. The brass shines bright enough to see your face in it.
